newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota, Honda fall on yen, car export report.
newsitem.headline: Toyota, Honda fall on yen, car export report.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp and Honda Motor Co Ltd fell on Thursday morning, hurt by strength in the yen and a report that the firms would limit their fiscal 1997/98 exports to the United States to previous-year levels, brokers said.
By the lunch break Honda had lost 180 yen to stand at 3,300, with 3.63 million shares traded, making it the fourth most actively traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
Toyota was down 190 yen at 3,290, also in heavy trade, with 3.27 million shares traded, making it the sixth most active issue.

The Japanese financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Wednesday that Toyota plans to export 430,000 vehicles to the United States in 1997, down from its original plan of 500,000 units but in line with 1996 export volume.
A Toyota spokesman in the United States said he expected total 1997 U.S. shipments to be flat or slightly down from the 432,000 units exported in both 1996 and 1995.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said Honda would export around 150,000 vehicles to the United States in 1997, down from its original plan of about 200,000 units.
But a Honda spokesman said that there had been no change of and that exports were expected to rise to 200,000 units in 1997, up from about 151,000 in 1996.
The Honda spokesman made the comment in Detroit on Wednesday.
